If improvements have been made to the natural drainage system on the upper land after the highway has been completed thereby increasing the quantity or rate of flow and creating a potential hazard because of an insufficient opening, the Division will make an evaluation of the new conditions. If this evaluation indicates that a flooding hazard does exist, corrective action will be taken within the limits of design practice.
2. Artificial Drainage
The highway facility shall be designed to provide the continued functioning of all intercepted artificial drainage systems. If the affected property owner, during the planning phase, desires to increase the capacity of the existing drainage facility either in size or in the number of the conduits to meet prospective future needs of the property, such adjusted facilities may be specified and constructed. The property owner, however, shall incur the costs of the adjustment that are in excess of the estimated cost to provide an adjustment satisfactory for the needs of the highway facility.
To serve agricultural land presently not drained, the Division, during the planning phase, will, upon request, install a proper strength sealed joint pipe line under the highway, "blind", at locations recommended by the Soil Conservation Service. The property owner shall incur all pipe and installation costs.
